q-125135.:question/problem: Let $b=\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}.$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $b$ and points the same direction.
q-125135.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{b}{|\,b\,|}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,b\,| & =\sqrt{{8}^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{64+36} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $b$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{b}{|b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot b \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -6\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{4}{5} \\ -\frac{3}{5}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

q-125138.:question/problem: Let $a=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 8\end{bmatrix}.$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $2a+b$ and points the same direction.
q-125138.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{2a+b}{|2a+b|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}2a+b & =2\cdot \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 8\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 8\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0+5 \\ 4+8\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 12\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|2a+b| & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{12}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{169} \\  & =13.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $2a+b$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{2a+b}{|2a+b|} \\  & =\frac{1}{13}(2a+b) \\  & =\frac{1}{13}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 12\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{5}{13} \\ \frac{12}{13}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

q-70409.:question/problem: Let $n=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $n$ and points the same direction.
q-70409.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{n}{|\,n\,|}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|n| & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{41}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $n$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{n}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{41}}\cdot n \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{41}}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{5}{\sqrt{41}} \\ \frac{4}{\sqrt{41}}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

q-70415.:question/problem: Let $r=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}$ and $s=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}.$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $3r+2s$ and points the same direction.
q-70415.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction., we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{3r+2s}{|3r+2s|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}3r+2s & =3\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+2\cdot \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -6\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}(-6)+0 \\ 3+(-6)\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|3r+2s| & =\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{45} \\  & =3\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $3r+2s$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{3r+2s}{|3r+2s|} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}(3r+2s) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

q-125137.:question/problem: Let $r=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -6\end{bmatrix}.$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $r$ and points the same direction.
q-125137.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{r}{|\,r\,|}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\,r\,| & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9+36} \\  & =\sqrt{45} \\  & =3\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $r$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{r}{|r|} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot r \\  & =\frac{1}{3\sqrt{5}}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -6\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

q-70419.:question/problem: Let $t=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ \sqrt{11}\end{bmatrix}$ and $v=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}.$ Find a unit vector that is parallel to $t+2v$ and points the same direction.
q-70419.:question/worked-solution:
Remember that to find a unit vector that is parallel to a given vector and points the same direction, we need to divide the given vector by its length:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{t+2v}{|t+2v|}\end{aligned}
$$

First, let's compute the sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}t+2v & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ \sqrt{11}\end{bmatrix}+2\cdot \begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ \sqrt{11}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}6 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-1+6 \\ \sqrt{11}+0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ \sqrt{11}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|t+v| & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(\sqrt{11})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide $t+2v$ by its length and get the following unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =\frac{t+2v}{|t+2v|} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(t+2v) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}5 \\ \sqrt{11}\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}\frac{5}{6} \\ \frac{\sqrt{11}}{6}\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
